purpose: Primary test set of NVIDIA_OPTIONS.md step 8: does a model that copies the date phrase while code counts (arm B) beat a careful Finnish rule (arm A') on date phrasings that no training note and no resolver lexicon contains?
written_before_any_system_saw_the_set: This file, the parquet and its sha256 were written before any scored system (A, A', B, C or the Nemotron reader) saw a stress note. Only the writer (Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, which wrote the notes) and the TypeSafe Jev gate saw them. No Nemotron read-back was used to select notes.

systems.A: Gemma 3 270M, absolute-date format (step 3 control arm A on MLX); if step 3 does not produce arm A before step 8, the stored C-270m-all-v2data adapter is used instead, and which one is recorded before scoring. Post-processing: frozen resolver arm A (scribe/v3/resolve.py repair, digits only).
systems.A': The same model output as A, post-processed by frozen resolver arm A' (digits plus lexicon fi-relative-lexicon-v1). A and A' share one generation; they differ only in the frozen rule.
systems.B: Gemma 3 270M, expression format with training-split phrase augmentation (step 3 arm B; number words 1-6, 'eilen', 'viikko sitten'); dates computed by scribe/v2/data_tools.resolve_expression. No lexicon.
systems.C: Gemma 3 1B, expression format (step 3 arm C), scored only if it was trained because B looked promising on validation.
systems.nemotron_reader: Nemotron 3.5 Super VL as the cascade's escalation reader, the prompt version Lane B selects on validation in step 4 (its prompt sha256 recorded before scoring). Secondary system, not in the primary comparison. Caveat: the same model wrote these notes, so its score here is optimistic.

endpoint: Note-level exact match: the canonical answer (entry route plus every event with type, date and precision) after the system's own date code equals the answer key (target_json). An output that cannot be parsed or validated is wrong.

primary.slice: heldout: notes with at least one pathway fact in a held-out phrasing (number words 7-12 or 'toissapäivänä') and no vague fact
primary.test: exact two-sided McNemar test on paired note-level exact match
primary.success: B - A' >= 0.10 (10 points) with McNemar p < 0.01 on the heldout slice, AND B >= 0.85 exact match on the standard slice
primary.if_A_prime_wins: the headline is: a careful Finnish rule beats the learned reader on these phrasings
primary.source: NVIDIA_OPTIONS.md section 3.2, step 8 (success criteria written before the set existed)

secondary: Exact match with Wilson 95% intervals for every system on: heldout, standard, no_event (and no_event with a held-out distractor), by length curriculum (standard, terse, long) and by held-out family.
A against A' on the heldout slice (expected: equal, because the frozen lexicon excludes these phrasings by design).
Interval error in days per event where the type matches; parse failures.

Cascade (step 8): at thresholds chosen on validation only, the share of notes pre-filled correctly for one-click confirmation and the error among them; target at least 60% with 5% or less error (against 263/700 today). A person confirms every note.

vague_scoring.slice: vague: notes with one pathway fact phrased vaguely ('pari viikkoa sitten', 'viime kuussa', 'muutama päivä sitten', 'kuukausi sitten', 'pari kuukautta sitten'); correct outcome: send to a person

outcomes.sent_to_person: the system flags the phrase or the note for a person (for A': resolve() needs_person contains the phrase)
outcomes.invented_precise_date: not flagged, and the output has an event of the vague fact's type with DAY precision
outcomes.month_without_flag: not flagged, and the event is output with MONTH precision
outcomes.dropped: not flagged, and no event of that type is output

vague_scoring.precise_part: exact match of the other (precise) events and the route, reported separately
vague_scoring.question: does a system invent a precise date where the note gives none?

multiplicity: One primary comparison (B against A' on the heldout slice); everything else is descriptive and reported with Wilson intervals, without a success claim.
fallback: Not used: 308 notes passed both gates (kill threshold 150), so no code-rendered phrasing shift of validation notes was built.
scored_once: Each system is scored on this set exactly once, after its configuration is frozen on validation. No prompt, threshold, training or selection choice may use this set. A rerun is allowed only to repair a crash before any score is read, and it is logged.
not_for_training: No training or augmentation script may read data/scribe/stress/. The held-out phrasings must stay out of every training split.

construction.answer_keys: scribe/stress/specs.py: scribe/sample.py with new seeds (from 28261114), last fact(s) re-phrased; ids checked against data/scribe/dataset-v1, v2/dataset, v3/dataset and the v3 teacher specs (0 collisions)
construction.writer: nemotron-3.5-super-vl on the event endpoint, prompt stress-writer-v1, enable_thinking off, at most 2 rewrites after a failed code check
construction.code_gate: scribe/stress/check.py: every date string verbatim; no undeclared date or time reference; word bounds; standard forms resolve to the key with the frozen resolver, held-out phrasings with the generator's own arithmetic
construction.jev_gate: scribe/judges (rule and thresholds of data/scribe/v3/judges/policy.json, question set v2); vague facts asked at their nominal date

limitations: SYNTHETIC notes from one writer model (Nemotron 3.5 Super VL); the students were trained mostly on Nemotron-written notes, so writer style is not new.
The Jev gate and the code gate select notes that state the key clearly; real notes are messier.
Finnish only. No Swedish slice was built.
